literal: If a person performs virtue without letting wasted days occur, that is a stone that blocks the path of their days of living.
translation: If one performs virtuous deeds daily without letting a single day go to waste, that practice will be a stone that blocks the path of future rebirths.
modern: ஒருவன் வீணான நாள் எதுவும் ஏற்படாதவாறு தினமும் அறச்செயல்களைச் செய்வானானால், அது அவனுடைய பிறவி வழியை அடைக்கும் கல்லாகும்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of daily, uninterrupted practice of virtue. The term 'வீழ்நாள்' refers to a wasted day, which in this context means a day spent without doing any good deeds. The poet suggests that if a person performs virtue ('நன்று') consistently every single day without fail ('படாஅமை'), that continuous practice acts like a heavy stone ('கல்') that blocks ('அடைக்கும்') the path ('வழி') of future births ('வாழ்நாள்'). Here, 'வாழ்நாள்' (literally, days of living) is used to represent the cycle of rebirths, and the blocking stone represents the cessation of this cycle through the power of accumulated virtue.
